match.reason: The closest point, on technological, geographic and institutional influences, treats place as one broad outside force, while the new point teaches how an owner weighs specific factors to choose a location, so it is a narrower and different idea.

draft.title: Choosing a location
card: Location is where a business sets up. The owner chooses it, and it affects both costs and sales.
Customers
a site close to customers, with good visibility, such as a busy street, can bring in more passing trade and more sales.
Suppliers and staff
being near suppliers can cut delivery costs and delays. Being near a pool of suitable workers makes hiring easier.
Rent and competitors
rent is a cost that differs from site to site, and busy sites often cost more. Nearby competitors may share the same customers, but they can also show that demand exists.
draft.remember: A good location balances the sales it can bring against the costs it adds.

a.q: Why might an owner pay higher rent for a shop on a busy main street?
opts: Passing customers may lift sales enough to cover the cost
Higher rent guarantees more customers will buy
Rent is the only cost that an owner can choose
Suppliers deliver for free to busy streets
a.why: A busy site has high visibility, so more people may see the shop and buy. That can make up for the extra rent. Higher rent does not guarantee sales, so the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what a busy street gives the shop in return.

b.q: Priya plans a bakery in a country town. Cheap rent is available on a quiet back street, or dearer rent on the main street. What is the best reason to choose the main street?
opts: Visibility to passing customers may raise sales
The rent is lower than on the back street
There will be no competitors on the main street
Suppliers will charge less for flour there
b.why: The main street gives visibility and more passing trade, which may raise sales above the extra rent. The tempting option about rent is wrong, because the main street costs more. Nothing in the case says there are no competitors.
b.clue: Which option is about gaining customers rather than saving money?

a.best: Passing customers may lift sales enough to cover the cost

b.best: Visibility to passing customers may raise sales

problems.detail: The why calls the 'guarantees' option 'the second option', but options are shown in random order and here it is third. Name the option by its content, not its position.
The clue ('Which option is about gaining customers rather than saving money?') gives the answer away. Only one option mentions customers, so students can pick it without understanding the trade-off.

The distractor 'Rent is the only cost that an owner can choose' uses 'only', and its absolute wording makes it easy to rule out without knowing the idea. It may be acceptable as a wrong option, but softer wording would test understanding better.

check.summary: The card, the remember line and both keyed answers are correct. Question a's why refers to 'the second option' by position, which won't match the shuffled order, and question b's clue gives the answer away.
